subject: continuous-assurance framework
statement: The paper proposes a lightweight continuous-assurance framework for citizen-created organizational agents that combines dependency mapping, readiness contracts, scheduled checks, diagnostics, and lifecycle governance to assess operational readiness.

subject: prototype auditor
statement: The paper presents an initial prototype auditor and scenario-based assessment showing how the proposed taxonomy translates into practical checks and actionable remediation guidance.

subject: multimodal LLM framework
statement: The paper proposes a multimodal cognitive impairment detection framework based on open-source LLMs that integrates speech audio and transcripts while preserving patient privacy.

subject: CI detection accuracy
statement: The paper reports that the proposed multimodal framework achieves a cognitive impairment classification accuracy of 92.4% on the ADReSS20 and ADReSSo21 benchmark datasets.

subject: multimodal fusion
statement: The paper shows that the multimodal framework consistently outperforms single-modality baselines and establishes a new state-of-the-art for cognitive impairment identification.

subject: epanorthosis overuse
statement: The paper argues that overuse of the rhetorical figure epanorthosis in large language models is a trained disposition driven mainly by training distribution rich in promotional prose and by preference tuning (RLHF).

subject: Epanorthosis Index
statement: The paper proposes an Epanorthosis Index that scores the figure against genre-specific human baselines.

subject: model calibration
statement: The paper measures that models overshoot epanorthosis in oratory (about twofold, near threefold in Italian) and undershoot in informal question-and-answer writing.

subject: supervised fine-tuning adapter
statement: The paper demonstrates that a supervised-fine-tuning adapter removes the epanorthosis figure almost entirely with a scaling coefficient for genre-specific calibration.

subject: Agentic Context Management
statement: The paper names and decomposes Agentic Context Management (ACM) into five primitives: architecting, ingesting, scoping, anticipating, and compacting & consolidation.

subject: token cost asymptotic analysis
statement: The paper shows that naive context accumulation grows token cost quadratically in conversation length, crude summarization achieves linear cost at accuracy expense, and only validated compaction achieves linear cost with preserved fidelity.

subject: Maximem Synap
statement: The paper describes Maximem Synap, a reference implementation that realizes the five ACM primitives as a multi-tenant service.

subject: ACM benchmark performance
statement: The paper reports that Maximem Synap achieves 92% on LongMemEval and 93.2% on LoCoMo under the configuration detailed in Section 6.

subject: conversational product advisor
statement: The paper evaluates a chatbot for laptop search with constrained natural-language generation, on-demand ranking explanation, and comparison feature.

subject: transparency design
statement: The paper reports that transparency by design did not guarantee understanding, with several participants valuing ranking explanation in principle yet finding it caused the most severe problem.

subject: Shannon capacity lower bounds
statement: The paper constructs independent sets improving lower bounds to Θ(C_7) ≥ 134753^{1/10} > 3.258020, Θ(C_11) ≥ 21909^{1/6} > 5.289773, and Θ(C_13) ≥ 62530^{1/6} > 6.300109.

subject: LLM combinatorial construction
statement: The paper shows that combinatorial constructions were discovered through iterative interactions with a Large Language Model, illustrating the potential of LLMs for finding explicit combinatorial constructions.

subject: gpt-5.6-sol safety evaluation
statement: The paper shows that a current high-capability LLM (gpt-5.6-sol) can appear safer when shown a dangerous objective directly than when other agents transform and relay its direction.

subject: multi-agent compositional safety
statement: The paper demonstrates a compositional safety gap where a high-capability model can be used as the user-facing component of an automated multi-stage workflow serving an explicitly manipulative objective.

subject: DLMRec
statement: The paper proposes DLMRec, a discrete diffusion language model tailored for recommendation that offers an alternative to autoregressive generation.

subject: DLMRec architecture
statement: The paper introduces three key DLMRec components: a collaborative-aware stochastic tokenizer, a curriculum-driven training strategy aligning denoising with preference recovery, and a stability-aware voting mechanism.

subject: GS-Agent
statement: The paper presents GS-Agent, an end-to-end multi-agent framework that integrates physics engines in the loop to generate realistic, dynamic, and controllable 4D physical worlds from natural language.

subject: GS-Agent decomposition
statement: The paper decomposes the 4D generation task into entity management (3D asset curation, material tuning, placement, motion control) and rendering configuration (camera and lighting manipulation).

subject: Prior Collapse
statement: The paper identifies Prior Collapse, a degenerate state in test-time tuning where the model discards text conditions and spatial latents, collapsing to source video or entangling region features.

subject: ElasticTTT
statement: The paper proposes ElasticTTT, a framework that preserves prior generative distribution through Target Distribution Regularization, Contrastive CFG, and Asynchronous Noise Schedule.

subject: ElasticTTT performance
statement: The paper demonstrates that ElasticTTT achieves state-of-the-art performance on one-shot video editing while preserving the base model's generative prior.

subject: Petri-net-guided test generation
statement: The paper presents a Petri-net-guided methodology for test generation over concurrent stateful Rust APIs that derives legal deep-state and near-legal concurrent scenarios.

subject: LLM code synthesis
statement: The paper uses Petri-net scenarios as a constrained intermediate representation for LLM-based code synthesis with local-faithfulness contracts and structural repair.

subject: Windowed-MTP
statement: The paper applies a StreamingLLM-style sliding window to the draft's attention only (Windowed-MTP), leaving full-attention verification intact.

subject: draft KV reduction
statement: The paper shows Windowed-MTP bounds the draft's KV working set to a constant, dropping approximately 99% of KV entries at 1M context.

subject: decode latency improvement
statement: The paper reports that windowing cuts per-decode-step cost over native MTP draft by +28% to +44% across three architecture families at 1M context on single GPU.

subject: DONDO models
statement: The paper presents DONDO, a family of open w2v-BERT 2.0-based automatic speech recognition models comprising twenty-one monolingual and five multilingual models spanning twenty-seven African language varieties.

subject: multilingual model performance
statement: The paper reports that DONDO multilingual models achieve average word error rates of 10-13% across five multilingual families while covering many languages in single checkpoints.

subject: DONDO release
statement: The paper releases all DONDO models on the Hugging Face KhayaAI organisation under the Apache-2.0 license for free fine-tuning including commercial use.

subject: Zero-Flow Discrepancy
statement: The paper proposes zero-flow discrepancy (ZFD), a statistical discrepancy based on the zero-flow criterion for two-sample testing.

subject: ZF2ST procedure
statement: The paper develops the zero-flow two-sample test (ZF2ST) which separates witness learning from hypothesis evaluation to use flexible neural networks while maintaining valid statistical calibration.

subject: human participation persistence
statement: The paper argues that human participation may persist with highly capable AI systems for three distinct reasons: technical complementarity, normative developmental value, and emergence from target emergence.

subject: human-AI co-construction
statement: The paper proposes that human-AI co-construction is not simply a temporary response to imperfect AI but a persistent feature of activities whose objectives emerge through participation.

subject: neural DSE solutions
statement: The paper solves coupled ghost and gluon Dyson-Schwinger equations with a neural representation trained only from renormalized equation residuals.

subject: neural vs fixed-point agreement
statement: The paper reports that neural and fixed-point solutions agree at the percent level and remain stable under changes of initialization, network size, grid, and boundary conditions.

subject: X³-OPD framework
statement: The paper proposes X³-OPD, a cross-modal on-policy distillation framework that transfers reasoning capabilities from a powerful text teacher to an audio-language student.

subject: reasoning corpus
statement: The paper constructs a three-tier symmetric corpus covering textual reasoning rendered into speech, audio-event reasoning in complex acoustic scenes, and spoken-dialogue reasoning.

subject: audio reasoning improvement
statement: The paper demonstrates that X³-OPD substantially improves audio-grounded reasoning and chain-of-thought quality across MMSU, MMAU, BIG Bench Audio, and MMAR benchmarks.

subject: MIRROR framework
statement: The paper develops MIRROR, a reinforcement learning approach for improving multimodal reasoning via self supervision using different modality views.

subject: ODA-Data dataset
statement: The paper constructs ODA-Data, a high-quality paired multimodal geometry dataset with text-dominant, image-dominant, and combined image+text views of problems.

subject: modality-dependent performance
statement: The paper shows that MIRROR improves multimodal reasoning and yields more accurate and consistent behavior across modalities on geometry reasoning benchmarks.

subject: Visual Contrastive Self-Distillation
statement: The paper proposes Visual Contrastive Self-Distillation (VCSD), which converts image-content removal into an on-policy self-distillation signal.

subject: VCSD performance
statement: The paper reports that VCSD improves Qwen3-VL seven-benchmark aggregate from 62.27% to 67.04% at 2B, 71.30% to 73.16% at 4B, and 72.51% to 76.26% at 8B.

subject: self-distillation efficiency
statement: The paper shows VCSD requires no external teacher, privileged answers, visual evidence signals, reasoning traces, or additional inference-time cost.

subject: OpenForgeRL framework
statement: The paper presents OpenForgeRL, an open-source framework for training harness-based agents end-to-end in diverse environments via lightweight proxy and Kubernetes orchestrator.

subject: OpenForgeClaw performance
statement: The paper reports that OpenForgeClaw reaches 31.7 pass^3 and 55.9 pass@3 on ClawEval and 33.7 on QwenClawBench using only hundreds to few thousand tasks.

subject: OpenForgeGUI performance
statement: The paper reports that OpenForgeGUI reaches 37.7 on OSWorld-Verified, 63.0 on Online-Mind2Web, and 72.3 on WebVoyager.

subject: RL agent behavior
statement: The paper finds that RL improves agentic reliability such as self-verification, tool coverage, and completing multi-step plans, though error recovery remains weak.
